title: From Student to PR: Exact Steps, Timeline & Costs (2026)
excerpt: Permanent residency is not decided at graduation — it is decided by choices you make before you even arrive. The exact steps, real timelines and true costs for Australia, UK, USA and New Zealand.

The Question You Should Ask Before You Even Apply to University

Most students plan their study abroad journey up to one point: graduation day. They research universities, compare tuition fees, prepare for English tests, and excitedly book their flights — but they rarely stop to think clearly about what happens after the degree is done. The students who build the best lives abroad are the ones who planned their PR pathway before they chose their course.

Permanent residency changes everything. It means you can stay indefinitely, work for any employer, access public services, bring your family, and eventually apply for citizenship. The difference between an international student who achieves PR and one who is forced to leave when their post-study visa expires is almost always one thing: planning. Specifically, choosing the right course, in the right city, in the right country, with the right work experience strategy during their studies.

⚠️
2026 is a policy-change year — the rules have shifted significantly Australia has tightened its post-study visa extensions. The UK is extending its settlement timeline from 5 to potentially 10 years. New Zealand has introduced new Green List fast-tracks. The USA's H-1B lottery remains deeply unpredictable. What worked for a student two years ago may not work for you today. Read this guide in full before making any decisions.

This guide gives you the exact steps, realistic timelines, and true costs of going from an international student to a permanent resident in Australia, the UK, the USA, and New Zealand — based on the rules as they stand in May 2026.

At-a-Glance: All 4 Countries Compared

Before diving into each country in detail, here is an honest comparison of the full student-to-PR journey across all four destinations. Use this to identify which country aligns best with your career goals, your timeline, and your risk tolerance.

🇦🇺

Australia — Points-Based PR, 3–5 Year Journey

Student Visa (500) → Subclass 485 → Subclass 189 / 190 / 491 → Permanent Resident

Australia's General Skilled Migration (GSM) system is the most structured and transparent PR pathway of any destination — which is exactly why it attracts so many international students. You earn points for your age, your qualification, your English level, your Australian work experience, and your field of study. Score 65 points and you are eligible to submit an Expression of Interest. Score 75 or above and you become genuinely competitive for an invitation in most occupations. The pathway is predictable — it rewards deliberate planning from day one.

The Exact Steps — Australia

1
Year 0 — Before You Arrive
Choose a CRICOS course on the Skilled Occupation List
Your occupation must appear on the Medium and Long-term Strategic Skills List (MLTSSL) to access the Subclass 189 independent visa. Nursing, IT, engineering, and accounting are among the strongest choices. Regional study adds 5 PR points before you even graduate.
2
Years 1–3 — During Studies
Study, work part-time in your field, build your points profile
Work up to 48 hours per fortnight during term. Try to secure work in your field of study — every year of skilled Australian work experience adds 5–10 PR points depending on duration. Your Australian qualification itself is worth 5 points.
3
At Graduation
Apply for Temporary Graduate Visa (Subclass 485) immediately
Apply as soon as your course completion is confirmed — do not wait. The 485 visa gives you 2–3 years of full-time work rights. This is your most critical window to accumulate work experience, build your points score, and submit your PR Expression of Interest.
4
Year 1–2 Post-Graduation
Get your skills assessed and lodge your Expression of Interest (EOI)
Your occupation must be assessed by the relevant skills assessment body (e.g. ANMAC for nursing, ACS for IT, Engineers Australia for engineering). Once assessed, lodge your EOI in SkillSelect. Invitations are issued based on your total points score.
5
Year 2–4 Post-Graduation
Receive invitation and apply for PR (Subclass 189, 190, or 491)
Subclass 189 is fully independent. Subclass 190 requires state nomination (lower point threshold but you must meet the state's requirements). Subclass 491 is a regional provisional visa that leads to PR after 3 years of regional living and working.
6
PR Granted — typically 3–5 years after first arriving in Australia
Permanent residency approved — you can live and work in Australia indefinitely
After 4 years of holding PR (with 1 year as a permanent resident), you become eligible to apply for Australian citizenship.

True Costs — Australia PR Journey

Subclass 485 (Temporary Graduate Visa)AUD 1,895
Skills assessment feeAUD 500–1,200
EOI lodgementFree
Subclass 189 / 190 application feeAUD 4,640
Migration agent (recommended)AUD 3,000–6,000
Estimated total (excluding agent)AUD 7,000–8,000
💡
The regional Australia fast-track Studying or working in a regional area adds 5 points to your score and unlocks the Subclass 491 provisional visa, which has lower invitation thresholds than the Subclass 189. Many international graduates achieve PR 1–2 years faster by choosing a regional city like Adelaide, Geelong, or Toowoomba over Sydney or Melbourne.
🇳🇿

New Zealand — The Fastest and Most Certain PR Pathway

Student Visa → Post Study Work Visa → Green List Residence / Skilled Migrant → PR

New Zealand's Green List is the most direct student-to-PR pathway available anywhere in the world in 2026. Tier 1 Green List occupations — including Registered Nurses, Doctors, Civil Engineers, IT Programmers, and several others — qualify for Residence from Work, a direct-to-PR pathway that requires no points test and no invitation. If you work in a Tier 1 occupation with a job offer meeting the median wage, you can apply for permanent residency almost immediately. The entire student-to-PR journey for a nursing graduate, for example, can be completed in as little as 2–3 years from arriving in New Zealand.

The Exact Steps — New Zealand

1
Before You Arrive
Confirm your occupation is on the Green List
Check Immigration New Zealand's Green List before choosing your course. Tier 1 occupations qualify for Residence from Work directly. Tier 2 occupations can still lead to PR through the Skilled Migrant Category but with additional requirements.
2
During Studies
Study, register with your professional body, build NZ experience
Work up to 25 hours per week (increased from 20 in 2026). For nursing students, complete your registration with the Nursing Council of New Zealand as soon as your degree is confirmed. Registration is the gateway to Green List PR.
3
At Graduation
Apply for Post Study Work (PSW) Visa — up to 3 years
The PSW visa gives you open work rights — any job, any employer. Apply within the specified window after course completion. For Master's graduates who studied full-time for at least 30 weeks, the PSW visa is valid for up to 3 years.
4
6–18 Months Post-Graduation
Secure skilled employment in your Green List occupation
Find a job in your registered occupation above the median wage threshold. Your employer does not need to be accredited for Tier 1 Green List applications. A standard employment agreement in your registered role is sufficient.
5
Year 2–3 — Tier 1 Green List Only
Apply for Residence from Work — direct PR, no points test
This is unique to New Zealand. Tier 1 Green List workers apply directly for permanent residency without a points calculation, without a lottery, and without waiting for an invitation. Processing typically takes 4–8 months.

True Costs — New Zealand PR Journey

Post Study Work VisaNZD 700
Professional registration (e.g. Nursing Council)NZD 400–800
Residence from Work applicationNZD 3,190
Immigration advisor (recommended)NZD 2,000–4,000
Estimated total (excluding advisor)NZD 4,300–5,000
🌿
New Zealand is the only country where PR is both fast AND certain In Australia, you compete against other applicants for a limited number of PR invitations. In New Zealand's Tier 1 Green List, there is no competition. If you meet the occupation, salary, and registration requirements, your PR application is approved. No lottery. No invitation. No waiting list.
🇬🇧

United Kingdom — Employer-Dependent, Longer Timeline

Student Visa → Graduate Route (2yr) → Skilled Worker Visa (5yr) → ILR → Citizenship

The UK's route from student to permanent resident is longer and more employer-dependent than Australia or New Zealand — but it remains one of the most valuable long-term pathways because of what it leads to: Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) and eventually British citizenship. The UK's 2026 immigration changes have made this pathway significantly more demanding. The salary threshold for the Skilled Worker Visa has risen to £41,700. English requirements have increased to B2. And the settlement timeline may extend from 5 to 10 years under proposed "earned settlement" rules.

⚠️
Major 2026 UK rule changes — read before you plan The UK government is introducing "earned settlement" rules from April 2026. Under the proposed changes, the ILR qualifying period may extend from 5 to 10 years for most Skilled Worker visa holders, with faster timelines possible for higher earners or those in public service roles. These changes are not yet law as of May 2026 — but if implemented, they significantly affect the UK's attractiveness as a long-term settlement destination.

The Exact Steps — United Kingdom

1
At Graduation
Apply for the Graduate Route visa — 2 years open work rights
Apply from inside the UK before your student visa expires. The Graduate Route gives you 2 years (3 for PhD) to work for any employer in any role. This is your job-hunting window. Crucially, time on the Graduate Route does not count toward the 5-year ILR qualifying period.
2
Year 1–2 Post-Graduation
Secure a job offer from a licensed UK sponsor at £41,700+
Your employer must hold a Home Office Sponsor Licence. Your role must be at RQF Level 6 (degree-equivalent) or above. Your salary must meet the higher of £41,700 or the "going rate" for your specific occupation code. NHS and education roles follow their own national pay scales.
3
Year 2–7
Switch to Skilled Worker Visa — your ILR clock starts now
Once you switch from the Graduate Route to the Skilled Worker Visa, your 5-year ILR qualifying period begins. You must not be absent from the UK for more than 180 days in any 12-month period. Your employer must maintain your sponsorship throughout this period.
4
Year 5+ on Skilled Worker Visa
Apply for Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR)
After 5 continuous years on qualifying visas, apply for ILR. You must pass the Life in the UK test, demonstrate B1 English, show no excessive absences, and earn at least £41,700 at the time of application. The ILR application fee is currently GBP 2,885 per person.
5
12 Months After ILR
Apply for British citizenship
After holding ILR for 12 months, you can apply for naturalization as a British citizen. You must have been physically present in the UK for the required period and must not have breached immigration rules at any point.

True Costs — UK PR Journey

Graduate Route VisaGBP 822
Skilled Worker Visa (3 years)GBP 819
Immigration Health Surcharge (3 years)GBP 3,105
Skilled Worker Visa extension (2 years)GBP 827
ILR application feeGBP 2,885
Life in the UK testGBP 50
British citizenship applicationGBP 1,630
Estimated total to citizenshipGBP 10,000–14,000+
🇺🇸

United States — Highest Reward, Highest Uncertainty

F-1 Student Visa → OPT / STEM OPT → H-1B (lottery) → EB Green Card → Citizenship

The USA offers the highest graduate salaries of any English-speaking country — but it comes with the most unpredictable path to permanent residency. The H-1B employer-sponsored work visa, which is the primary route from international student to US Green Card, is subject to an annual lottery. Even highly qualified graduates from top universities are not guaranteed selection. This means that unlike Australia, New Zealand, or even the UK, there is no reliable, plannable pathway from student to US permanent resident that you can map out in advance. The rewards are extraordinary. The certainty is not.

The Exact Steps — USA

1
At Graduation
Apply for OPT — 12 months of work authorization
All F-1 graduates can apply for Optional Practical Training (OPT) — 12 months of work authorization directly related to your major. Apply through your university's international student office at least 3 months before graduation. Work must be in your field of study.
2
STEM graduates only
Apply for STEM OPT Extension — 24 additional months
If you studied a STEM subject (Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics), you can extend OPT by a further 24 months — giving you 36 months total of US work authorization. Your employer must be enrolled in the E-Verify system to sponsor STEM OPT.
3
Year 1–3 on OPT
Find an employer willing to sponsor your H-1B
The H-1B is the most common work visa for international professionals in the USA. Your employer applies on your behalf. The H-1B is capped at 85,000 new visas per year and is subject to a random lottery, run each April. Selection is not guaranteed even for well-qualified candidates.
4
Year 3–10+ (if H-1B is secured)
Employer sponsors your Employment-Based Green Card (EB-2 or EB-3)
After several years on H-1B, your employer can sponsor you for a Green Card through the EB-2 (advanced degree) or EB-3 (skilled worker) categories. Wait times vary enormously by nationality — from under 1 year to over 10 years depending on your country of birth and the visa category.
5
Green Card Granted
After 5 years as a Green Card holder, apply for US citizenship
A Green Card gives you permanent US residency. After 5 years (3 years if married to a US citizen), you can apply for naturalization and US citizenship.
💡
The USA is a long-term bet — not a 5-year plan For graduates who make it through the H-1B lottery and into a well-paying STEM career, the USA can deliver exceptional life outcomes. But the process is long, employer-dependent, and cannot be guaranteed. Students who need a more predictable path to permanent residency should seriously weigh Australia or New Zealand alongside the USA.

True Costs — USA PR Journey

OPT application (EAD card)USD 410
STEM OPT extensionUSD 410
H-1B (employer pays, but included for context)USD 3,000–6,000
Green Card (I-485 adjustment of status)USD 1,440
Immigration lawyer (highly recommended)USD 3,000–8,000
Estimated total (personal costs only)USD 5,000–10,000+

5 Decisions You Make During Your Studies That Determine Your PR Outcome

Permanent residency is not decided at the end of your studies — it is decided by dozens of small choices you make along the way. These are the five that matter most.

  • Course choice: Only occupations on the relevant skilled lists qualify for PR in Australia and New Zealand. Choosing a course that does not align with any shortage occupation is the single biggest planning error international students make. Check your occupation code against the skilled occupation lists before you apply — not after you graduate.
  • City vs regional study (Australia): Studying in a regional Australian city adds 5 PR points and unlocks the Subclass 491 pathway. Over thousands of applicants competing for limited metropolitan invitations, those 5 points can mean the difference between receiving a PR invitation and waiting an extra year. Choose your campus location strategically, not just for lifestyle reasons.
  • Work during studies: Every year of skilled Australian work experience adds points. Part-time work in your field of study during your degree — rather than unrelated hospitality work — means you arrive at graduation with a head start on PR points that other graduates spend an extra year trying to accumulate on the 485 visa.
  • Professional registration timing: In New Zealand, your Green List PR application cannot proceed until you are registered with your relevant professional body. For nurses, this means completing NCLEX or OSCE assessments and meeting the Nursing Council's requirements. Begin this process in your final semester — not after graduation — to avoid months of delay.
  • Absence management: In the UK, you must not be absent for more than 180 days in any 12-month period during your qualifying residency. Many international students are unaware of this rule until it threatens their ILR eligibility. Keep a careful record of every trip outside the UK from the day your Skilled Worker Visa begins.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which country gives international students the fastest path to permanent residency?
New Zealand offers the fastest and most certain PR pathway for international graduates in 2026, specifically through its Tier 1 Green List. Graduates in qualifying occupations such as Registered Nursing, Civil Engineering, or IT Programming can apply directly for permanent residency through Residence from Work without a points test or lottery. For nursing graduates in particular, the full journey from arriving in New Zealand to holding permanent residency can be as short as 2–3 years.
Does time on the UK Graduate Route count toward my ILR qualifying period?
No — time spent on the UK Graduate Route does not count toward the 5-year qualifying period for Indefinite Leave to Remain. Your ILR clock only starts when you switch to a qualifying long-term visa such as the Skilled Worker Visa. This is an important distinction: a student who spends 2 years on the Graduate Route before switching to Skilled Worker will need a minimum of 7 years in the UK before becoming eligible for ILR, not 5.
What happens if I fail the H-1B lottery in the USA?
If your H-1B application is not selected in the lottery — which happens to a significant proportion of applicants each year — your employer can reapply in the following year's lottery. In the meantime, you must remain on a valid visa status. Options include extending OPT (if still within the STEM OPT period), switching to another visa category, or returning to your home country. Some students in this situation choose to pivot to Australia or New Zealand, where the PR pathway is more predictable.
Can I apply for Australian PR while still on my 485 post-study visa?
Yes — and this is in fact the most common and recommended approach. Many international graduates lodge their Expression of Interest in SkillSelect during their 485 visa period, accumulate skilled work experience points, receive an invitation, and are granted PR while still legally residing in Australia on the 485. The 485 visa exists specifically to give you time and opportunity to build the work experience and points score needed for a competitive PR application.
